name: American Cancer Society: Hope Lodge, rides to treatment and the helpline (charityevals, 2025-26)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: Hope Lodge lodging, Road To Recovery rides and the helpline and information for patients in the US.
summary: The American Cancer Society's patient services in the US, year to March 2026: free lodging at its Hope Lodge communities (565,000 nights), Road To Recovery volunteer rides to treatment (93,000 rides for 7,500 patients) and its 24/7 helpline (284,000 calls, chats, emails and texts) with online information and peer support, about $235m of its $426m patient-support line (the rest, prevention and screening promotion, is in the research-and-policy model). Lodging and rides are valued as money saved, on the site's log scale for patients' households, plus a small judged chance that they keep a patient's treatment on track; information and support as a small, short wellbeing gain scaled down from trials of psychosocial support for people with cancer. The result, about 0.004 years of healthy life per $1,000, is low because a few thousand dollars saved is a small gain to a US household and a call is a small dose of support; every branch is discounted for missing data, since ACS counts nights, rides and contacts but measures no outcomes. How often lodging and rides keep treatment on track and how much a call or a page helps are the biggest uncertainties, and the result is mostly uncertainty.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

rows.explainer: Volunteer drivers give the rides; ACS pays for coordination staff, the scheduling platform and, in some areas, paid ride partners. About $9m; 2% to 8%.

rows.label: Hope Lodge: log-consumption gain per person
rows.explainer: A one-off saving in the year of treatment.

rows.label: Hope Lodge: cancer deaths averted per stay
rows.explainer: Free lodging lets some patients take treatment at a distant specialist centre or finish a course they would otherwise cut short. A review of the literature on distance and cancer care (Ambroggi et al., The Oncologist 2015) found that longer travel goes with more advanced disease at diagnosis, less adequate treatment and worse survival in most of the studies it covers, all observational; no trial measures lodging. If 5% of guests would otherwise have had worse or incomplete treatment and that costs 4% of them their life, 0.002; 0 to 0.008.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: price of a ride to treatment (round trip)
rows.explainer: A round trip of about 20 miles by taxi or rideshare in the US; $20 to $60.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: value per person in the household
rows.explainer: A year's rides, shared over the household.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: log-consumption gain per person
rows.explainer: Over the treatment year.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: cancer deaths averted per patient given rides
rows.explainer: Transport barriers cause missed and delayed treatment (Syed, Gerber and Sharp, J Community Health 2013: reported by 3% to 67% of patients across studies); delayed treatment raises mortality a few percent per month of delay for common cancers (Hanna et al., BMJ 2020). If one in ten ride users would otherwise miss or delay treatment and that costs 3% of them their life, 0.003; 0 to 0.01.

rows.label: Helpline: gain in wellbeing per person (standard deviations)
rows.explainer: Psychosocial and educational interventions for people with cancer improve distress and quality of life by about 0.25 standard deviations over several sessions (Faller et al., J Clin Oncol 2013); one or two calls with a cancer information specialist are about a tenth of that dose, as the British Heart Foundation's helpline (0.03 to 0.3 of a trial's dose). 0.025, 0.0075 to 0.075.

rows.label: Other information and peer support: gain in wellbeing per person (standard deviations)
rows.explainer: Reading trusted pages or a peer visit is about a hundredth of a trial's dose, as the British Heart Foundation's reading dose (0.003 to 0.03): 0.0025, 0.00075 to 0.0075.

rows.label: Helpline and information: share of the people helped who are patients or their close caregivers
rows.explainer: The trials' effect is for people with cancer; the helpline and pages also serve people worried about symptoms, students and professionals. 70%, 50% to 85% (the British Heart Foundation's information branch counts only patients, 22% of its readers, because most of its readers are the general public).

rows.label: Years the wellbeing gain lasts
rows.explainer: Support around a diagnosis or treatment helps for the months it lasts; 6 months, 3 to 12.

rows.label: Helpline: WELLBYs per person
rows.explainer: Standard-deviation years at the site's shared rate.

rows.label: Other information: WELLBYs per person
rows.explainer: As the helpline.

rows.explainer: Averaged over everyone reached, for reading.

rows.formula: (lodge_households * household_size * lodge_value_per_person + rides_patients * household_size * rides_value_per_person) / people_reached
rows.explainer: For reading.

rows.label: Log-consumption gain per person reached (for reading)
rows.explainer: For reading; the branches count their own.

rows.label: Illness averted per person
rows.explainer: The health gain is counted as deaths averted below; illness averted is left at 0: a patient kept alive lives on with the illness of cancer and its treatment, so better-completed treatment may add illness as well as remove it (7% of US cancer DALYs are illness).

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached (for reading)
rows.explainer: For reading.

rows.label: value of a cancer death at 70 or older (United States, units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's five-year weights for 70-74 and 75-79 (their mean) and for 80 and over (80-84; 85 and over has the same weight), mixed by the share of these deaths at 80 or older (WHO GHE 2023).

rows.label: value of a cancer death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: Every death the site counts is valued by the age it happens at (docs/normalization.md, decision 2026-10-31 #4): GiveWell's moral weights by age over the ages of cancer deaths (in the United States, WHO GHE 2023, facts: death_ages), 50-69 at the 50-74 band and 70 and over at the five-year weights, times the value-of-a-life slider.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (for reading)
rows.formula: (lodge_raw * lodge_evidence_adj + rides_raw * rides_evidence_adj + info_raw * info_evidence_adj) / (lodge_raw + rides_raw + info_raw)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Hope Lodge: evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: The money saved is counted at ACS's own prices with the cash-equivalent share; the health part's doubt is in its range.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: As Hope Lodge.

rows.label: Helpline and information: evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: The dose is in the effect rows; this is trust in the trials' effect itself: psycho-oncology trials are small and their pooled effects shrink in larger and better-blinded studies, and the people who call or read are self-selected, so their gain may differ from trial participants'. 0.7, 0.4 to 0.95.

rows.label: Hope Lodge: share of the saving that wouldn't have come anyway
rows.explainer: Some hospitals have their own subsidised lodging, some guests would have stayed with relatives for free or found a cheaper room, and some would have travelled daily: 70%, 50% to 90%.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: share of rides not otherwise free
rows.explainer: Medicaid covers non-emergency transport for its members, some hospitals offer rides, and some patients would have been driven by family; 60%, 40% to 85%.

rows.label: Helpline and information: share not otherwise got from the care team or other sources
rows.explainer: Patients also get information from their oncologists, nurses, the National Cancer Institute's Cancer Information Service and other charities: 55%, 30% to 80%, as the British Heart Foundation's information branch.

rows.label: Counterfactual (for reading)
rows.formula: (lodge_raw * lodge_counterfactual_adj + rides_raw * rides_counterfactual_adj + info_raw * info_counterfactual_adj) / (lodge_raw + rides_raw + info_raw)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Hope Lodge: ACS's share of the resources
rows.explainer: Land leases and patient lodging given in kind are other people's resources (Convention 2).

rows.label: Hope Lodge: in-kind share of its cost
rows.explainer: In-kind gifts over the branch's spending.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: volunteer hours per ride
rows.explainer: Driving to the patient, to the clinic, waiting or returning: about 2 hours, 1 to 3.

rows.label: Road To Recovery: value of the volunteers' time
rows.explainer: At the site's US volunteer-hour value (Independent Sector, 2025).

rows.formula: program_spend * rides_share * overhead_ratio / (program_spend * rides_share * overhead_ratio + rides_volunteer_value)

rows.label: Helpline and information: ACS's share of the resources
rows.explainer: Delivered by ACS's own staff.

rows.label: Share of the resources (for reading)
rows.formula: (lodge_raw * lodge_attribution_share + rides_raw * rides_attribution_share + info_raw * info_attribution_share) / (lodge_raw + rides_raw + info_raw)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Attribution share (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only; each branch applies its own.

rows.label: Share of reported reach that gets the help as counted (information branch only)
rows.explainer: ACS's own counts of contacts: some are repeat or misdirected contacts, and some are bookings for lodging or rides already counted in those branches. Applied to the information branch only: a night or ride counted is delivered. 90%, 80% to 100%.

rows.label: Funging: others would have paid anyway (below 1)
rows.explainer: ACS's lodging and rides are funded by restricted gifts and events that might otherwise go elsewhere in cancer care; little leverage. 0.95, 0.85 to 1.05, the template's default.

rows.label: lodge: discount for missing outcome data
rows.explainer: Thin: ACS counts nights, rides and contacts but measures no outcome, and the effect is judged from other studies (Convention 12).

rows.label: rides: discount for missing outcome data
rows.explainer: Thin: ACS counts nights, rides and contacts but measures no outcome, and the effect is judged from other studies (Convention 12).

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Not counted: the company of other patients at Hope Lodge and its staff's support (wellbeing, left out to avoid counting the lodging twice), the volunteers' own wellbeing from driving, navigation that gets patients to treatment sooner after a helpline call, the caregivers' time saved. Harms: none known beyond the funging above. 10%, -5% to 30%.
